article_title: The effect of haptic virtual reality simulation training before clinical endodontic practice on student performance and perception.
citation: Şimşek Emine, Satar Selimcan. (2026). The effect of haptic virtual reality simulation training before clinical endodontic practice on student performance and perception. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09577-x
title: HVRS as a complementary simulation-based learning environment grounded in experiential learning and deliberate practice
description: The article frames haptic virtual reality simulation as a training tool that "combines three-dimensional visualization with tactile feedback," offering students "a realistic, interactive, and repeatable learning environment." It positions preclinical training models, including HVRS, as "structured learning environments grounded in experiential learning, deliberate practice, and simulation-based education principles." The mechanism proposed is that repeated practice in a controlled setting reduces cognitive load during the transition to clinical practice, allowing students to automatize procedural steps before treating real patients. The authors explicitly frame HVRS as complementary to, not a replacement for, conventional preclinical education.
requirements: A single instructor following a standard protocol
Supervision by a faculty member or researcher during training
Simulator providing immediate on-screen validation of access cavity preparation
constraints: Cannot completely replace traditional phantom-based preclinical training
Direct transfer of skills acquired in a virtual environment to real patient conditions may be limited
target_learners: fourth-year dental students treating patients for the first time in endodontics
target_learning_goals: fine motor skills and hand–eye coordination
